hooks.command: CMD=$(python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d.get('tool_input',d).get('command',''))" 2>/dev/null || true); case "$CMD" in *grep*|*rg\ *|*ripgrep*|*find\ *|*fd\ *|*ack\ *|*ag\ *) [ -f graphify-out/graph.json ] && echo '{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "additionalContext": "graph.json exists (local knowledge graph). For STRUCTURAL questions about the codebase (how X flows end to end, what calls/depends on Y, blast radius of a change, which subsystem owns Z): run  graphify query \"<q>\" ,  graphify explain \"<node>\" , or  graphify path \"<a>\" \"<b>\"  FIRST -- faster and far cheaper than grep. Query by GRAPH VOCABULARY (real node labels / god-nodes like Crowd, ChunkManager, mulberry32, worldHash, ChaseCamera), not raw prose. IN the graph: src/ (+ models, worldgen), bin/, the HTML entry points, and project docs (ARCHITECTURE, CLAUDE, README, ROADMAP, CHANGELOG, DEBUGGING, PLAN, .claude/{agents,commands,rules} + design notes, openspec/specs, openspec/schemas, verification/). NOT in the graph: openspec/changes/, .claude/skills/ (three.js packs), node_modules, most images -- for those, or to read specific lines, just grep; an empty graph result for an out-of-scope path means nothing, not absence."}}' || true ;; esac
